_exportRoutes_note: Optional. Leave exportRoutes empty and every pulled file type lands under exportRoot, which is the original behaviour. Add routes when different file types belong in different places - raw .job files are datalogger state, while the .csv and scans a surveyor exported are deliverables. 'from' is 'export' (the collector's exportSubPath) or 'root' (the project folder on the device, where Trimble Access keeps .job). Each route gets its own leg in the compare view. Use 'overwrite' collision where filenames must stay exactly as exported - it still never destroys anything, a clash lands as 'name (2).ext' - and note that 'prefix' renames a scan's '<name> Files' folder, which severs the .jxl from its point cloud.

exportRoutes._note: The trailing fixed segment (a company folder here) sits under the dated part, so files land in <year>\<month>\OURCO. Duplicate detection still scopes to the whole month, so a file someone later moved into a different company's folder is not pulled again.
exportRoutes.name: QC survey data

exportRoutes._supersede_note: A .job is a live database the crew adds to all day, so a newer copy replaces the backup instead of landing beside it. Without this, every sync of a job still being worked in leaves one more copy. Leave it off (the default) for exported files: two .csv sharing a name are two different surveys and both must be kept.
exportRoutes.name: Job files

_driveMap_note: Drive letters the tool creates with subst when they are missing, so a fresh login never breaks a sync. S: is the whole team folder, which is what lets every path above be short and identical on every machine. Targets are tried in order and %ENVVAR% is expanded - prefer %OneDriveCommercial% to a C:\Users\<name>\... path, or the config only works for whoever wrote it. A letter that already resolves is never touched.
_defaults_note: The baseline every collector starts from. Edit it HERE - the GUI deliberately cannot write it, so nobody can turn a one-off tweak into everyone's default by clicking. Reset to defaults (Advanced) puts one collector back on it; collectors already set up keep what they have until you do.

defaults._jobRetentionDays_note: Days of recent jobs the 'Tidy jobs' button must never touch. It only ever removes a .job that is older than this AND has a date in its filename AND has a verified backup copy - all three, or it stays.

_collectors_note: Do not hand-write these. Plug a collector in and press Detect - the serial is read from the USB descriptor (or, for a USB stick, from the volume), the name you give becomes the export filename prefix, and these settings are copied from defaults.

collectors._note: A USB stick as a collector. serial is VOL- plus the volume serial, so it is found wherever Windows mounts it; model is the volume label.
collectors.name: USB-01
